blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: streets and boundaries

items.t: County Line / Glen Valley is the Fraser River floodplain strip in northeast Langley Township at the Abbotsford line.
272 Street is the County Line boundary with Abbotsford, and River Road runs along the Fraser through Glen Valley.
The provincial dike inventory lists a separate Glen Valley Dyking District map sheet (sheet 19).
Fort Langley lies west along River Road, and Trinity Western University's Langley campus at 22500 University Drive sits south of the valley floor.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: the housing stock

items.t: Housing is detached homes and farmhouses on large rural and floodplain lots, not strata complexes.

Historic Hassall House, built in 1917 inside Glen Valley Regional Park, is described by Metro Vancouver as a typical 1920s rural farm residence and the site of Glen Valley's first store, post office and wharf.
Township zoning for floodplain parcels includes the Rural Floodplain Zone RU-4 named in Township council reports.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: rules that affect buyers

items.t: ALR rules govern most valley-floor parcels, including house size and extra residences.
The principal residence cap in the ALR is 500 m² total floor area, with larger homes needing a Non-Adhering Residential Use application.
Township Official Community Plan Schedule 3 Streamside Protection and Enhancement areas require habitat protection along creeks, as applied in Township reports for RU-4 land near the Salmon River.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Glen Valley Regional Park is split by the municipal line: Poplar Bar, Duncan Bar and Crescent Island are part of the park within the City of Abbotsford, managed by the Fraser Valley Regional District and operated by Abbotsford.
Metro Vancouver warns the riverbank in the park is eroding and undercut, water levels are tidal and can change rapidly, and dogs must be leashed.
Hassall House is closed to the public and rented as a private residence.
Nathan Creek in Glen Valley has been a focus of habitat work along the dike near the end of 80 Avenue, per Township-related reporting read.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: development and new projects

items.t: The Glen Valley and Salmon River Flood Mitigation project is the active infrastructure project touching this area.
Township capital-projects material lists dike widening and raising along the Fraser River with status Planning among its major projects.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: costs and taxes

items.t: Township flat-rate utilities are billed separately from property taxes.
For 2026, the Township flat rate is $779.96 for water and $716.47 for sanitary sewer for a single-family home, with garbage base rate $226.00 plus cart charges.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: getting around

items.t: River Road and 272 Street are the through routes; there is no rapid transit on the valley floor.
The nearest regional transit hub is Carvolth Exchange, where TransLink added weekday afternoon service on the 555 Port Mann Express toward Carvolth in its Fall 2026 changes.

blocks.text: County Line / Glen Valley: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the Glen Valley dike sheet, floodplain zone and creek setbacks for the exact lot.
The provincial dike inventory maps show pump stations, flood boxes, low dikes and hazard-concern areas regulated under the Dike Maintenance Act.
Streamside Protection areas under OCP Schedule 3 can limit building envelopes near Nathan Creek and other watercourses.

blocks.text: Jared's take on County Line / Glen Valley
Out in Langley’s northeast corner, toward the Abbotsford border, County Line / Glen Valley is farm country on the south shore of the Fraser. It’s some of the prettiest rural land in Langley.

faq.q: What is being done about Glen Valley flooding?
faq.a: A multi-phase Township project with Kwantlen First Nation and the Rivershed Society of BC is upgrading flood infrastructure.

faq.q: Can I fish or launch a boat in the park?
faq.a: Yes, within Metro Vancouver park rules at Glen Valley Regional Park. Metro Vancouver lists fishing, canoeing/kayaking and a canoe/kayak launch among the park's features, and its brochure states fishing needs a Tidal Waters Sport Fishing Licence and car-top boats can launch at the Poplar Bar parking lot area.

faq.q: Which school district serves the valley?
faq.a: School District 35 (Langley) serves both Langley Township and Langley City. SD35 publishes catchment maps and a School Locator Tool, and buyers should run the exact address through the locator because rural east Langley catchments differ by street and feed different elementary and secondary schools.

faq.q: Can I build a second residence on an ALR lot?
faq.a: Only under the ALC's additional-residence rules. The Commission's policy allows generally one residence per parcel, an additional residence only where the ALR Use Regulation permits it, and otherwise a Non-Adhering Residential Use application that the Commission must not grant unless the extra residence is necessary for a farm use.

faq.q: What is County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: A Fraser Valley board sub-area in the Township of Langley — rural acreage country of equestrian estates, hobby farms and multi-acre parcels. It is one of eleven Langley sub-areas in the SnapStats data, on the Township side of the combined Langley board community (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: How active is the County Line Glen Valley market?
faq.a: Very thin in the published data: in September 2026 the sub-area recorded 0 detached active listings with 1 sold (sales ratio NA, as published — a sale against zero snapshot inventory, not a trend), and 0 Condos & Townhomes listings with 0 sold. Langley community context for the same month was 449 detached listings / 64 solds and 699 attached listings / 128 solds (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: What is the median price in County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: SnapStats does not publish a sub-area median — medians exist at community level only, and the Langley community medians for September 2026 were $1,345,000 detached and $611,000 for Condos & Townhomes. Those are community figures, not this sub-area's figures; the live feed's first page ran from $1,975,000 to $7,999,900, which is feed data, not a median (SnapStats, September 2026)
